---
title: "The scratch bucket"
description: "Cloud storage on the hub for trying things out. Files are deleted after 7 days."
---

The hub comes with an S3 **scratch bucket**, `{{< var hub.scratch >}}`. It is
a good place to write a test Icechunk store to cloud storage, rather than to
your home directory. You do not need to set up any credentials, because the hub
already has them.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Files in the scratch bucket are deleted 7 days after you upload them.**
Everyone on the hub can read and write it, so stay inside your own folder.
Do not put anything there you need to keep, and never put credentials there.
:::

## Your folder

The hub sets an environment variable, `SCRATCH_BUCKET`, that points to a
folder named after your GitHub username:

```python
import os
scratch = os.environ["SCRATCH_BUCKET"]
scratch    # 's3://nmfs-openscapes-scratch/<your-github-username>'
```

## Write, list, read and delete

```python
import s3fs

fs = s3fs.S3FileSystem()             # uses the hub's credentials

fs.pipe(f"{scratch}/hello.txt", b"hello")   # write a small file
fs.ls(scratch)                              # list your folder
fs.cat(f"{scratch}/hello.txt")              # read it back
fs.rm(f"{scratch}/hello.txt")               # delete it
```

To upload a local file or folder, use `fs.put("local.nc", f"{scratch}/local.nc")`.
For a folder, add `recursive=True`. `fs.ls` raises an error on an empty folder,
so write something first.

## An Icechunk store in the scratch bucket

You can write an Icechunk store here almost as easily as to a local folder.
Only the storage setup changes:

```python
import boto3
import icechunk

bucket, prefix = scratch.removeprefix("s3://").split("/", 1)
creds = boto3.Session().get_credentials().get_frozen_credentials()   # the hub's credentials

storage = icechunk.s3_storage(
    bucket=bucket,
    prefix=f"{prefix}/my-store",
    region="us-west-2",
    access_key_id=creds.access_key,
    secret_access_key=creds.secret_key,
    session_token=creds.token,
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
Why not `from_env=True`? On this hub, Icechunk does not pick up the hub's
credentials by itself, and you get `AccessDenied` (tested 2026-11-13 with
icechunk 2.3.1). Passing them from `boto3` works. They expire after about an
hour, so rerun the cell if a long session starts failing.
:::

Chapter 6, [Building a store](../slides/06-build.qmd), covers the rest. Or ask
your agent: *"write the smoke-test store to my scratch bucket instead of a local
folder."*
